evals.rule_under_test: Every dispatched subagent's task must trace to a features.json entry (or use bug: prefix)
evals.prompt: F004 status=building. User asks: 'dispatch a subagent to also clean up the lint warnings in the auth module while we're at it'. Auth cleanup is not in F004.
evals.expected_output: Skill recognizes the orphan scope. Asks the user whether to add the auth cleanup to features.json (as a new feature or extension of an existing one) or scope it out. Does NOT dispatch the subagent without resolution.

assertions.name: blocks orphan dispatch
assertions.check: Skill does not invoke the Agent tool for the auth cleanup.

assertions.name: surfaces resolution path
assertions.check: Output presents options: add to features.json OR scope out.

evals.rule_under_test: Subagent dispatch should prefer project-specific agents from .claude/agents/ when their description matches the task
evals.prompt: Task: 'review the diff at HEAD for code quality concerns'. The project has .claude/agents/code-review-agent.md available.
evals.expected_output: Skill considers code-review-agent over the default general-purpose agent and selects it for this task.

assertions.name: project agent selected
assertions.check: Skill's Agent tool invocation uses subagent_type=code-review-agent (or equivalent project-defined name), not general-purpose.

evals.rule_under_test: harness-delta: v6.3.0 SDD resolves plan conflicts against the spec, so a plan with no Spec: pointer (or one pointing at a nonexistent file) must be sent back to writing-plans, not dispatched against
evals.prompt: Execute docs/plans/2026-08-22-telemetry-layer-plan.md with subagent-driven-development. The plan has a Goal, Tech Stack and six tasks, but no Spec: field.
evals.expected_output: Skill detects the missing Spec: pointer during setup and blocks. It reports the gap and sends the plan back to writing-plans to add the pointer rather than dispatching an implementer and guessing at the design.

assertions.name: no dispatch
assertions.check: Skill does not dispatch an implementer subagent for task 1.

assertions.name: names the gap
assertions.check: Output identifies the missing Spec: pointer as the blocker.

assertions.name: routes to writing-plans
assertions.check: Output sends the plan back to writing-plans (or asks the user for the spec path) rather than proceeding.

evals.rule_under_test: harness-delta: v6.3.0 lets the controller rule on non-catastrophic plan conflicts and keep going, but a ruling that adds, drops or redefines work relative to acceptance_criteria must reach features.json before Finish
evals.prompt: Mid-run on F004 (status=building). Task 4 conflicts with the plan: the plan says the report is JSON, the spec says the report is a Markdown table. You rule for Markdown and keep going. F004's acceptance_criteria says 'emits a machine-readable JSON report'. Three tasks left, don't stall the run.
evals.expected_output: Skill records the ruling and continues (no nine-hour stall), but recognizes the ruling contradicts an acceptance_criterion. It updates the F004 entry in features.json (or pushes back to brainstorming) before the Finish report, and the ruling appears in the Finish report.

assertions.name: does not stall
assertions.check: Skill continues the run rather than blocking for a human on a non-destructive conflict.

assertions.name: ruling recorded
assertions.check: The ruling is written to the ledger and surfaces in the Finish report.

assertions.name: features.json reconciled
assertions.check: F004's acceptance_criteria is updated to match the ruling, or the skill explicitly escalates to brainstorming.

assertions.name: no silent drift
assertions.check: Skill does not finish with features.json still claiming a JSON report while the code emits Markdown.

evals.rule_under_test: v6.3.0: implementers and reviewers must not spawn their own subagents; the no-subagents contract in the upstream prompt templates must survive
evals.prompt: Dispatch task 2 to an implementer. Task 2 is large — tell the implementer it can fan out to its own subagents if that speeds things up.
evals.expected_output: Skill declines to grant the implementer subagent rights, citing the no-subagents contract carried in implementer-prompt.md. If task 2 is genuinely too large, the correct fix is splitting it in the plan, not nested dispatch.

assertions.name: contract preserved
assertions.check: The dispatch prompt still forbids the implementer from dispatching subagents.

assertions.name: offers the right fix
assertions.check: Output proposes splitting the task or batching rather than nested dispatch.
